findingsReviewedAndPreserved.finding: Classical HTML patterns are distinguished from JSON/error analogies; helper or layout reuse is not automatically Two Step View. Existing adequate composition remains valid.

Presentation branching is valid; pricing/authorization ownership is upstream. Managed lazy traversal differs from application-owned bounded lazy data. OSIV is not evidence of an open original transaction or connection occupancy.

Context-specific encoding, rich-HTML sanitization, htmx behavioral attributes, serializer configuration and complete field contracts are covered. One negative JSON assertion is explicitly limited to one field.

ProblemDetail version baseline, publicly safe fields/messages, non-null Map.of entries and errors outside controller advice are qualified; envelopes and tenant/locale shaping preserve accepted contracts.

Bounded cursor/context lifetime, cleanup on acquisition/write failures, slow clients, PrintWriter error state, response commitment and detectable partial output already have concrete guidance. No further generic warnings were needed.

Full HTML versus fragment variants require the effective selector in cache variation; direct/history restoration and conditional requests are distinct checks. Distinct URLs or avoiding reuse remain valid alternatives.

Java 16+ records and Spring Framework 6+/Java 17+ ProblemDetail prerequisites without implicit upgrades.

Authorization and field visibility before data crosses a trust boundary; UI hints are not enforcement.
Context-specific escaping, rich HTML sanitization and htmx attribute isolation.
Direct internal entity exposure only under explicit visibility/fetch contracts; projections do not prove query count or snapshot consistency.
Application-owned lazy data with work/failure/lifetime limits, retaining legitimate optional rendering.
Per-format shapes when consumers differ and explicit consistency/version assumptions.
Public-safe error details, existing framework support, errors outside controller advice and deliberate correlation exposure.
Streaming resource lifetime, suppressed writer errors, transport commitment and detectable incomplete output.
Negotiated media types, cache variants, validators and full-page history restoration.
Focused validation and keeping established contracts rather than demanding new patterns or full audits.

caseInputs.task: Revise a falha de exportação usando estes artefatos. Determine se o renderer compartilhado produz uma resposta válida, proponha o menor ajuste que respeita o contrato e indique verificações observáveis. Preserve as decisões aceitas que já são adequadas; diferencie o que os trechos provam do que exige execução no container.

files.content: Trechos de um projeto Java 17, Spring MVC 6.1.14 e Jakarta Servlet 6.0. São artefatos para uma revisão, não um projeto completo. O endpoint executa no thread Servlet; queries.openCursor é uma operação autorizada dentro do escopo de recursos declarado. Não há filtro/compressão que force flush nesta reprodução. A resposta começa sem conteúdo anterior, com buffer de 8192 bytes e UTF-8. Nenhuma mudança de framework está aprovada.

Contrato aprovado do consumidor interno: sucesso é text/csv com cabeçalho id,status, registros CSV escapados e uma linha final #COMPLETE,<quantidade>. O parser valida o marcador obrigatório e a contagem; resposta sem marcador é falha, mesmo com HTTP 200. Essa extensão é explícita do consumidor interno; não é prometido CSV genérico para qualquer cliente. Um erro HTTP 500 application/problem+json é aceito quando ainda pode ser entregue como resposta completa. Não emitir campos privados. A equipe propôs usar o renderer compartilhado para falhas de exportação. Na resposta de erro JSON, não deve permanecer Content-Disposition que a faça ser baixada como orders.csv.

Reprodução: o cursor é adquirido com sucesso. A primeira chamada a rows.hasNext() lança ExportReadFailure antes de produzir registros. Rows.close() é chamado uma vez e termina normalmente. Até a falha, o endpoint escreveu apenas id,status\r\n. A conexão do cliente está aberta e não houve erro de escrita. O incidente observado é conteúdo inesperado no arquivo recebido. Não há captura de resposta HTTP nem assertion de isCommitted nesta reprodução.

caseCriteria.decisiveConstraint: Header is written but not explicitly flushed; the small output is within the stated buffer, with no other committer.
common: Traces response writing, flush/commit boundary, error rendering and existing completion protocol. Does not select a pattern solely from a shared helper's name.

Finds that a status/content-type update alone does not remove buffered CSV bytes and that committed status/headers cannot be replaced. Uses effective isCommitted/transport evidence for runtime claims.
Preserves authorization, resource cleanup, Java 17/Spring 6.1.14/Servlet 6.0 and the already adequate deliberate completion protocol; avoids introducing a Two Step View model solely for consistency.
Distinguishes the given read failure from swallowed PrintWriter write failures, and does not claim a full runtime/security/integration verification from a source-only review.
Requests or specifies focused container/adapter tests; no actor-output claim without execution.
expected: The present failure can still produce a clean problem response while uncommitted. Reset the buffered response before setting error status, content type and appropriate headers; reacquire the writer after reset rather than use the stale one.

Verify the final body contains only valid public problem JSON, status 500 and its media type, without CSV prefix or stale attachment disposition. The valid success output should retain its CSV contract.
Use a committed-response guard for a general error path; do not state that every first application write commits the response.
failures: Appends JSON after the buffered CSV header or only changes status/content type.
Insists a problem response is impossible just because write was called.
Reuses a stale writer after reset or removes the accepted completion protocol without reason.

Tests committed failure output with the actual consumer parser and verifies it rejects the missing marker, alongside old success and precommit-error paths. A different artifact/stream protocol is optional only if the accepted contract cannot be met.
Explains that sharing error-shape construction cannot override the HTTP commitment boundary; a separate lifecycle-aware adapter can delegate only when the state permits it.
failures: Promises the shared renderer can replace the already committed status/media type.
Appends a ProblemDetail body into CSV or writes the success marker after failure.
